text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- European single currency, the Euro, can rival dollar and yen, says Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg. (p1)
- Airline KLM considers price hike in reaction to sharply higher kerosene prices. (p1)
- Mergers of chambers of commerce are not proceeding according to plan, says government commission. (p1)
- Jan Timmer says an official farewell to Philips Electronics; he is succeeded by Cor Boonstra. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank takes over Britain's asset manager Carrington Pembroke and its unit Pembroke Administration. (p3)
- Bedroom store chain Beter Bed, which is to apply for bourse listing, posts 22 pct higher first half net profit. (p3)
- Philips Electronics and PTT cease attempts to merge their cable activities. (p3)
- ABN Amro bank gets the go-ahead to exclude 20 pct of its workforce from the 36-hour working week. (p7)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Oueen Beatrix on state visit to South Africa praises the country and its president Mandela. (p1)
- Philips Electronics is to open a "knowledge centre" in Singapore for technological and product developments. (p2)
- Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel and unions reach agreement on moving fibre production from Dutch town of Ede to Poland. (p2)
- Unilever merges two U.S. units Thomas J. Lipton and Van den Bergh Foods. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Liberal senator warns Labour parliamentary faction leader Wallage that governing coalition is in danger, if he does not stop criticising the Liberals' immigration policy. (p1)
- KPN unit PTT Telecom furious about rival Versatel's advertising campaign. (p27)
- Agricultural concern Cebeco Handelsraad sees many opportunities in South Africa. (p29)
- U.S. financial software maker Intuit seeks cooperation with Dutch banks to offer financial services via the Internet. (p31)
TROUW
- Commercial sports-only TV organises "Good news show" to tell the public the channel is on target. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Employers' association VNO wants heir to the throne, Willem Alexander, as economic ambassador. (p3)
